dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: The present days are quick to pass, but their stories are easily told — and few remain who may still recall the histories of old. Thus, we must pass down stories, so that battles and sages, gods and adepti are always remembered.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Now, lean close in your seats and lend me your ears, for I shall speak now of Rex Lapis.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: This tale begins two thousand years prior. The days then were not ones of peace, as you and I remember...

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Liyue then was a place of contention between countless gods. Foul demons roamed the land, and the people could find no words to describe their agony...

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Then, Rex Lapis arose as the head of the adepti, and saved the people from calamity...

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: Indeed, Rex Lapis was the Prime of Adepti, and by his side stood the Seven Guardian Yakshas, mighty even amongst their kin.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: It was then that Rex Lapis fought a great battle against the sea monster, the tyrant of the oceans.

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: That sea monster was a true titan, with a head as broad as Mt. Tianheng... Just think about it! How huge must its whole body have been, then?

dialogues.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
dialogues.text: With its maw wide open, the sea monster lunged towards Liyue Harbor, intent on swallowing it and all its people whole!

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: ...But you must recall, dear guests, that Rex Lapis was a god, and he was not afraid!

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: And he commanded the adepti in a loud voice, and gathered rock unto him within one hand — then, he summoned forth a rain of stones as large as buildings, beating that sea monster bloody!

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: Those rocks then plummeted into the seas, and pinned themselves to the very ocean floor like so many long spears. Today, we know this place as the Guyun Stone Forest.

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: And upon seeing this, the adepti and the yakshas fell upon the creature also, and with weapons and adeptus arts they frustrated the monster, filling its hide with wounds...

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: Ah, but now, wickedness stirred in the creature's black heart. "O, this wretched Lord of Geo! I shall ruin his city, and then we shall see if he is more my foe, or their protector!"

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: So thinking, the sea monster churned the oceans, and sent forth a great wave hurtling towards the harbor.

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: Even the adepti were dismayed, and ceased their assault for but an instant. But they looked to Rex Lapis, and lo! He was calm and unmoved.

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: Why was Rex Lapis undaunted, you ask?

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: Listen closely, for all will be revealed in the next telling...

response.speaker: Tea Master Liu Su
response.text: ...But you must recall, dear guests, that Rex Lapis was a god, and he was not afraid!
